en.explanation:
Partial roasting of chalcopyrite gives

2CuFeS + O CuS + 2FeS + SO

2CuFeS + 4O CuS + 2FeO + 3SO

Since iron is more electropositive than copper, so its sulphide is oxidised in preference. CuS remains mostly unaffected and the small amount of CuO formed on oxidation, reacts with FeS to give back CuS.

2CuS + 3O 2CuO + 2SO

CuO + FeS CuS + FeO
en.comprehension: Copper is the most noble of the first row transition metals and occurs in small deposits in several countries. Ores of copper inculcated chalcanthite (CuSO . 5HO), atacamite (CuCl(OH)), cuprite (CuO), copper glance (CuS) and malacite (Cu(OH)CO). However, 80% of the world copper production comes from the ore of chalcopyrite (CuFeS). The extraction of copper from chalcopynite involves partial roasting, removal of iron and self-reduction.
